source: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS), Haushaltsbudgeterhebung (HABE) / Household Budget Survey, Table T20.02.01.00.12 'Haushaltseinkommen und -ausgaben nach Einkommensklasse', pooled survey years 2012-2014
notes: REAL PRIMARY DATA from BFS HABE, but VINTAGE CAVEAT: this table (T20.02.01.00.12) pools three survey years (2012-2014) and is the most recent full-category income-class breakdown located in permanent/stable xlsx form on BFS's dam-api asset server. BFS's national-AVERAGE table is refreshed annually (2022 vintage available at https://dam-api.bfs.admin.ch/hub/api/dam/assets/32666961/master, used for the 2022 all-household average in de_evs.json-style cross-checks) but its by-income-class disaggregation was not found updated past 2012-2014 in machine-readable table form during this session; a 2022 BFS press release (https://dam-api.bfs.admin.ch/hub/api/dam/assets/32526563/master) references quintile splits (e.g. 'top fifth of single-person households under 65 had CHF 8028/month vs bottom fifth CHF 1706/month') but only as prose summary statistics, not a full category-by-quintile table -- so those 2022 figures are NOT included here, to avoid mixing table vintages inconsistently. Treat this file's absolute CHF figures as reflecting c. 2013 price levels, not 2024 -- apply Swiss CPI inflation adjustment (~2013->2024 CPI increase ~appx 5-7% cumulative, source: BFS consumer price index) if a nominal-2024 comparison is required; this file leaves that adjustment undone per the 'do not fabricate' instruction (only real, retrieved values are included). Income brackets are 5 unequal-width CHF/month bands (<5021, 5021-7336, 7337-9978, 9979-13687, >=13688) but each holds ~20.0% of Swiss households (BFS source row 89: 19.99%-20.02% per bracket), so they are treated here as an approximate QUINTILE breakdown (q1=lowest to q5=highest). CATEGORY MAPPING (BFS COICOP-derived categories -> v2 schema): housing = 'Wohnen und Energie' (housing + energy/utilities combined, BFS does not separate them at this table's granularity); food_at_home = 'Nahrungsmittel und alkoholfreie Getränke' (food & non-alcoholic beverages); food_away = 'Gast- und Beherbergungsstätten' (restaurants AND hotels/lodging combined -- BFS does not separate dining-out from short-stay accommodation at this level, so this OVERSTATES pure food-away-from-home versus BLS's narrower definition); healthcare_oop = 'Gesundheitsausgaben' (health expenditure, out-of-pocket; excludes mandatory basic health-insurance premiums 'Krankenkassen: Prämien für die Grundversicherung', which BFS classifies as a MANDATORY TRANSFER expenditure alongside taxes/social-security contributions, not as consumption -- this matches BLS's OOP convention of excluding premiums from healthcare consumption); transport_work = null (BFS 'Verkehr' is not split into commute vs. discretionary use); transport_total = 'Verkehr' (all transport: vehicle costs, public transit, etc.); apparel = 'Bekleidung und Schuhe' (clothing & footwear); communications = 'Nachrichtenübermittlung' (postal, telecom); personal_care = null (folded into 'Andere Waren und Dienstleistungen' / other goods & services, not separately broken out at this table's granularity); education = null (not a distinct line item in this table version; BFS does track education spending in more granular COICOP-12-category tables not retrieved in this session); childcare = null (not a distinct category); voluntary_savings = null (BFS reports 'Sparbetrag' -- a residual savings BALANCE = income minus expenditure, not a voluntary-contribution expenditure flow comparable to BLS's retirement-savings concept; including it here would conflate a balancing item with a discretionary expenditure category, so left null per do-not-fabricate); entertainment = 'Unterhaltung, Erholung und Kultur' (entertainment, recreation & culture); other = 'Wohnungseinrichtung und laufende Haushaltsführung' (furnishings/household operation) + 'Alkoholische Getränke und Tabakwaren' (alcohol & tobacco) + 'Andere Waren und Dienstleistungen' (other goods & services, incl. personal care) -- combined residual bucket. avg_income_before_tax = 'Bruttoeinkommen' (gross income: all earned + pension + transfer income). avg_income_after_tax = 'Verfügbares Einkommen [3]' (disposable income = gross income minus mandatory transfer expenditure, i.e. minus social-security contributions + taxes + mandatory basic health-insurance premiums) -- BFS's disposable-income definition NOTABLY INCLUDES mandatory health-insurance premiums as a deduction (unlike most countries where health premiums are a voluntary/discretionary expenditure), which is a Swiss-specific institutional feature (mandatory individual health insurance) worth flagging for any cross-country comparison. housing_owner_share = null (not published by income class/quintile in this table; BFS separately reports a NATIONAL-AVERAGE renter-household share of ~61.7% i.e. owner share ~38.3% for 2022, per dam asset 32666961 row 94, but not disaggregated by income bracket).
